If you are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless, VA can help connect you with resources such as homeless shelters or faith-based organizations; you can call the National Call Center for Homeless Veterans at 877-424-3838. A Social Security Benefit Verification Letter may also be used as proof for housing assistance or mortgage purposes.

rows.answer: Yes, you may be able to get disability benefits from VA if you meet the requirements for a specific exposure or service situation. For Agent Orange exposure, this must be true: You have an illness VA believes is caused by Agent Orange, called a presumptive disease. At least one of these must also be true: You came into contact with Agent Orange while serving in the military, or you served in or near the Korean DMZ between September 1, 1967, and August 31, 1971, or you served in the Republic of Vietnam between January 9, 1962, and May 7, 1975. For Camp Lejeune water contamination, you must have served at Camp Lejeune or MCAS New River for at least 30 cumulative days from August 1953 through December 1987, did not receive a dishonorable discharge, and have a diagnosis of one or more listed presumptive conditions.
